title: Li Shufu, who started schools before making cars: The AI era will give birth to a batch of new-type universities

content_html:
At the 2026 Xinwei Education Forum, Li Shufu, Chairman of Geely Holding Group, made a bold judgment: the talent-training system of traditional universities can no longer keep up with the needs of the AI era, and “the AI era will inevitably give rise to a group of new universities that match this era.”

Before building cars, build schools first

Behind this statement is an old Geely tradition. Li Shufu reiterated the idea of “being both an enterprise and a school”: in the early days of Geely’s automotive industry venture, it relied on Geely Technician College and Geely Technical School—talent, technicians, and skilled workers came first, and cars came later. Today, Geely has formed a multi-level education system ranging from secondary and higher vocational education to undergraduate and graduate education, including Geely University, Sanya University, Xiangtan Institute of Technology, and other schools.

Will universities repeat the old path of department stores?

His concern about the form of universities is captured in a direct analogy: traditional universities are like traditional department stores and supermarkets, while universities born in the AI era are like Alibaba, Tencent, JD.com, and ByteDance. Years ago, Shanghai No. 1 Department Store and Hangzhou Jiefang Road Department Store were once so glorious, but today they have been squeezed into a corner by e-commerce—“completely different starting points, completely different results.” Under the new model, students can arrange their learning pace according to their own preferences and actual circumstances.

He also warned against over-mystifying AI: knowledge in databases does not mean everyone has mastered it, and no matter how smart large language models become, it does not mean everyone automatically becomes smarter. Training methods and learning content must keep pace with the progress of the times. Facing the dual challenges of new globalization and geopolitics, Geely will work with its schools to expand its talent development scale globally, enroll undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral students, and cultivate a new type of globalized talent.
